description: The COVID-19 Community Mobility Reports chart how visits to, or time spent in, categories of places changed during the pandemic, by country and sub-national region, relative to a baseline. Categories are retail and recreation, groceries and pharmacies, parks, transit stations, workplaces and residential. Google built them from aggregated, anonymised Location History of users who had turned the setting on, with differential privacy noise, to help public health officials. Each value is a daily percentage change against the median for the same weekday in the five weeks from 3 January to 6 February 2020. Reports stopped on 15 October 2022 (last created 17 October 2022); the historical data stay available as a global CSV, per-region CSVs and PDF reports, free of charge once users accept the Google Terms of Service. Caveats: the baseline ignores seasonality and fell after COVID-19 had begun in some regions, Google advises against comparing regions or reading day-to-day changes, gaps appear where data were too thin, and the Location History panel is not a random sample. The transit stations series gives a daily, near-global record of how public transport use fell and recovered under a pandemic shock, for resilience and demand-scenario studies of transit systems; related records are the Istanbul hourly public transport ridership and the Korea transit card ridership data.
name: Google COVID-19 Community Mobility Reports (2020-2022)
